title: Plan your living room around the sofa
subtitle: A practical way to test the layout before choosing a sofa, chairs and tables.
coverAlt: Cream upholstered seating and nesting tables in the Crafting Corner showroom
excerpt: Use a floor plan, a tape outline and the way you spend an evening at home to choose a sofa layout that fits your living room.
seoTitle: How to Plan a Living Room Around Your Sofa | Crafting Corner
intro: The sofa usually claims the most floor space in a living room, and its position shapes everything around it. Before comparing fabrics or arm styles, work out where you want to sit, what you want to face and how people will move through the room. The cream seating and nested tables in our showroom photograph offer one example of a grouped arrangement. Use your own room’s proportions to decide what to borrow from it.
sections: Start with the room’s daily routes

Sketch the positions of doors, windows and furniture you plan to keep. Then draw the paths you take on a normal day, such as the route from the entrance to the balcony. Mark where doors and drawers swing open. A sofa against the longest wall can still make the room hard to cross if its arm projects into a busy route.

Think about the best view from the seat. A room used for conversation may work well with chairs facing the sofa at an angle. If you watch television most evenings, try sitting where the sofa would go and notice whether windows produce glare.
Mark the footprint on the floor

Use removable tape to mark the outside dimensions of your shortlisted sofa, including its arms. Add the coffee table and any chair you expect to keep. Walk through the room, try sitting down and check whether you can reach a table without leaning forward. With a corner sofa, mark the return on the actual side where it will sit and check that it leaves a clear route.

If the layout feels crowded, try a straight sofa with one movable chair and a side table. Compare both arrangements with the tape in place. The option with less furniture can still offer a comfortable seat for everyone who uses the room most often.
Try the seat and look at the fabric in context

Sit as you would at home. Notice whether your feet rest comfortably, whether the back supports you and how the arms feel when you lean on them. If two people will use the sofa daily, ask both to try it. Seat depth and back angle can feel very different from one person to the next.
View upholstery samples in daylight and under the kind of lamp you use at home. Bring a photo of your existing rug or curtains, and ask how the specific fabric should be cleaned.
Measure the route into the room

Record the narrowest doorway, lift opening and any tight turn on the stairs. Ask the supplier for the delivery dimensions of the exact sofa and confirm which parts, if any, can be detached. Bring the sketch, photos and measurements to the showroom so the conversation can begin with your room.

title: Plan a bedroom around your bed
subtitle: Fit the bed, storage and bedside essentials into a room that feels easy to move through.
coverAlt: Classic wood-frame bed with pale upholstery in the Crafting Corner showroom
excerpt: Use the bed frame’s full dimensions, the swing of wardrobe doors and your bedside routine to lay out a bedroom that works every day.
seoTitle: How to Plan a Bedroom Around Your Bed | Crafting Corner
intro: Start a bedroom plan with the outside dimensions of the bed frame. Mattress sizes are useful when shopping for linen, but a headboard, low footboard or upholstered surround can extend considerably beyond the mattress. Our showroom photograph shows how a curved frame contributes to a bedroom’s character. In your room, its size also affects where you can walk, reach the lights and open storage.
sections: Draw the fixed features first

Sketch the bedroom and mark the door, window, sockets and wardrobe. Open each door and drawer and note where you stand to use it. If the room also needs a dressing table or a desk, mark the space a chair needs when pulled out.

Try the bed against more than one wall on the sketch. Consider the walk from the doorway to your usual side of the bed and the route from the bed to the wardrobe. Check that curtains can move freely and the headboard leaves access to switches or sockets you use.
Leave room to move and make the bed

Mark the frame’s footprint with low-tack tape or cardboard. Walk around it and try reaching the far side as if you were changing the sheets. Open a nearby wardrobe drawer with someone standing beside you. Everyday movements can reveal a tight spot that is easy to miss on a floor plan.

If you are looking at a frame with drawers underneath, ask which way they open and how far they extend. Allow space to stand and open them fully. For a lift-up base, ask to see the mechanism on the exact model you intend to order.
Choose bedside pieces around what you use

List the items you reach for most often at night. A book, a glass of water and a reading lamp may need only a modest top, while other belongings are easier to keep in a drawer. Compare the table height with the top of the mattress once the frame, mattress and any topper are accounted for.

Two matching tables can give the bed a balanced appearance. If one side sits by a doorway, a narrower piece on that side may fit better. Similar lamp heights or finishes can tie the two sides together.
Check the details before ordering

Ask for a drawing or written dimensions for the bed frame, including its height and any parts that extend beyond the mattress. Check access to your home as well as the bedroom door. Bring a floor plan and a few photos if you want to discuss the relationship between the bed, bedside cabinets and storage at the showroom.

title: Prepare a brief for custom furniture in Mohali
subtitle: Turn your room measurements, reference images and finish preferences into a conversation about one piece.
coverAlt: Ornate cream seating and a coffee table in the Crafting Corner showroom in Mohali
excerpt: Bring a clear brief to your custom furniture consultation in Mohali. Start with the room, then agree dimensions, materials, samples and delivery details.
seoTitle: Custom Furniture in Mohali: How to Prepare a Brief | Crafting Corner
intro: A useful custom furniture brief can fit on a page. Name the piece you need, explain how you will use it and show the part of the room where it will sit. A console for a narrow entrance might need a shallow top and drawers that are easy to reach. A seat for a reading corner might need an arm at the right height. That detail gives the showroom conversation something specific to work with.
sections: Bring a simple plan and photographs

Measure the available width, depth and height, then photograph the room from the doorway and from either side of the intended position. Show skirting, sockets, switches or anything that projects from the wall. Note which measurements are approximate and agree who will confirm the final site measurements before the piece is specified.

For a console or cabinet, write down what will go on top and what needs to fit inside. For a seat, describe who will use it most often, where their feet should rest and whether it needs to sit alongside pieces you already own.
Explain what you like in each reference

Bring a few images and say what draws you to each one. It might be a curved leg, a muted finish or the shape of an arm. The carving in our showroom detail photo is one way to point out a decorative feature. If you like the silhouette but want a quieter finish, write that down so one decision does not get mistaken for the other.
Review dimensions, materials and samples together

Ask for the dimensions and materials of the specific piece to be recorded in writing. If it has doors, drawers or upholstery, ask what hardware or fabric is included and how you can assess it. Look at samples in daylight and in the kind of lighting used in your room. Keep the name or reference for the sample chosen so it can be checked against the quotation.
Agree the practical details before committing

Confirm the scope of the quotation, what needs approval and who will handle delivery or installation. Measure any tight doorway, lift or stair turn and share it before the delivery plan is agreed. Ask how later changes would affect the agreed specification, price or timing.

A useful starting email includes the piece you have in mind, the room dimensions, a couple of photographs, a rough budget and any fixed dates. Bring the same information if you are visiting the Crafting Corner showroom in Mohali.
